The updated prototype is live at **http://maker:4001** (refresh the page). Here's how I'd like you to try the new pieces — I'll walk you through them in a sequence so each one is easy to judge:

**1. Save two links first, so there are existing tags to work with.** Save `https://css-tricks.com/snippets/css/a-guide-to-flexbox/` — when the details appear, notice the **site icon and small page preview** now collected at the top, flip the **"Read later"** switch on, add a tag like `css`, and add it. Then save `https://figma.com` with a tag like `design`.

**2. Now test tag suggestions.** Start saving `https://stripe.com` and, in the Tags field, begin typing `c` — you should see your earlier `css` tag suggested so you can reuse it with a click instead of retyping. This is me guessing at how suggestions should behave: they match as you type and you click to accept. Tell me if that's the interaction you pictured.

**3. Now test duplicate recognition.** Paste `https://css-tricks.com/snippets/css/a-guide-to-flexbox/` again (the first link) and press Save link. Instead of creating a second copy, it should recognize it, show an amber "you've saved this before" notice, and open your **existing** bookmark for editing — change the note and confirm; the original updates in place rather than a duplicate appearing.

A couple of assumptions I made that I want your read on:

- **The read-later badge:** in the list I mark read-later items with a small "Read later" tag on the card. Is a marker like that what you'd expect, or did you picture it living only in the separate unread view we'll build next?
- **The preview image size:** I kept it as a small thumbnail on the right of each card so it aids scanning without dominating — does that size feel right?

Try those three flows and tell me your reactions — and especially whether the duplicate-recognition behaviour feels reassuring rather than annoying.
